name: Geometric Illustration
visualIdentity: Recognizable figures, objects, and environments built from a limited geometric vocabulary. Shared angles, proportions, line weights, and palette keep scenes coherent; forms can split, assemble, and resize while retaining identity and visual balance.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to illustrated narratives, concept transitions, brand idents, logo stories, posters, report covers, and design system introductions. It can support videos or interactive HTML when the subject benefits from clear geometric forms and structured staging.
limitations: Avoid organic, blobby morphs, continuous motion without holds, and changes that break the subject’s identity or balance. Scrollytelling or chapter transitions need meaningful narrative steps. Suitability of the style for a particular topic is inferred; no specific subject, duration, or aspect ratio is supplied.
palette: Optional four-token suggestion: background #F3EFE4, foreground #253849, accent 1 #BF6D45, accent 2 #638878. Use discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Task, brand, reference, and existing semantic colors take precedence and must retain exact values and roles. Accent-on-background contrast is below the normal-text target, so use accents decoratively and place body text on a readable existing backing; verify actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Use reusable groups with explicit pivots and hierarchy; split, rotate, assemble, and morph around shared coordinates. Preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections, and reading holds. For video, derive every state from seekable composition time. Interactive HTML may use scroll to drive coherent chapter or story states, and pointer position for bounded character gaze only when suitable facial layers exist; provide neutral recovery and reduced-motion/static states as appropriate. These interactions are optional, not style requirements.
audio: Unspecified for the style. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the particular subject and audience; honor supplied audio requirements. Synchronize and mix with picture, keeping speech intelligible and avoiding clipping or competing vocals.
assetRequirements: Use SVG for scalable shapes and paths; Canvas or procedural tools can build parameterized geometric arrangements. Optional tldraw can author editable diagrams, and Paper.js can construct or combine vector paths. Load assets before animation; preserve source colors and contours. Facial layers or a rig are required for gaze, while flattened images may not support separate movement. Exact task assets and copy are unspecified.
combinations: Works alone. Geometric shape morphs can extend decomposition into transitions if they retain shared angles, palette, pivots, and holds. Swiss grid typography can align text and forms, using only the primary palette and flush-left sans type; do not import Swiss red, centered text, or decorative type. These combinations are suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: Select visual construction and motion methods by fidelity and action; SVG, Canvas, and GSAP are suitable options, with optional specialist tools only as needed. HyperFrames is the primary scene, timing, media, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, and record why. Keep renderer, motion engine, and pipeline responsibilities distinct; verify direct, backward, and out-of-order seeks, representative frames, full playback, audio sync, and loop continuity.
